info.title: dally
info.description: A job queue server. See docs/design.md and docs/semantics.md for how delivery works.

get.summary: The process is up and can reach storage.

`GET /v1/messages?queue=&status=&before=&limit=`, newest first. Pass the
response's `next` as `before` to get the following page.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only messages older than this one: pass the previous page's `next`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many messages, up to 500. Defaults to 50.

409.description: The lease or status does not allow this

patch.summary:
`PATCH /v1/messages/{id}` with `{"delay": "1h"}` or `{"run_at": "..."}`.
An empty object runs it now.

get.summary: `GET /v1/queues`: every queue with its message counts.

200.description: Every queue with its message counts

put.summary:
`PUT /v1/queues/{queue}`: creates the queue or replaces its settings.
Fields left out get their defaults, not their current values.

post.summary:
`POST /v1/queues/{queue}/dead/retry` with an optional `{"ids": [...]}`.
Without ids, retries every dead message in the queue.

requestBody.description: Optional; without ids, every dead message is retried

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only messages older than this one: pass the previous page's `next`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many messages, up to 500. Defaults to 50.

post.summary: `POST /v1/queues/{queue}/messages` takes one message or an array of them.
post.description:
One message: `201 Created` with the message, or `200 OK` with the existing
message if its idempotency key was already used.

An array: `200 OK` with `{"messages": [{"created": bool, "message": ...}]}`
in the same order.

200.description: The existing message, if its idempotency key was already used; or the results of a batch

requestBody.description: Optional; defaults to one message and no waiting

lease.description: The lease token from the poll.

Backoff.description:
Exponential backoff with jitter: attempt `n` waits about
`min(base * 2^(n - 1), cap)`, give or take 20%.

base.description: The delay after the first failed attempt.

ErrorBody.description: The error body every endpoint uses.

message.description: For people. May change between versions.

LeaseToken.description:
The token that proves a worker holds a message. It changes every time the
message is leased, so a worker whose lease expired cannot ack a message
that was handed to someone else.

lease.description: The proof that this worker holds it.

Leased.description: A message handed to a worker, with the token it needs to ack or nack it.

attempts.description: How many times it has been leased.

finished_at.description: When it reached a finished status.

idempotency_key.description: The key that prevents duplicates, if one was given.

last_error.description: The error reported by the last failed attempt.

lease_expires_at.description: When the current lease expires, while it is running.

max_attempts.description: How many attempts it gets before it is marked dead.

status.description: Where it is in its lifecycle.

MessageId.description:
A message id. Ids are UUIDv7, so sorting them sorts messages by creation
time.

NackRequest.description: What a worker reports when an attempt fails.

error.description: What went wrong. Shown in the UI and kept on the message.

lease.description: The lease that proves the worker holds the message.

retry_in.description: Retry after this delay instead of the queue's backoff.

Page_Message.description: One page of a listing, newest first.

attempts.description: How many times it has been leased.

finished_at.description: When it reached a finished status.

idempotency_key.description: The key that prevents duplicates, if one was given.

last_error.description: The error reported by the last failed attempt.

lease_expires_at.description: When the current lease expires, while it is running.

max_attempts.description: How many attempts it gets before it is marked dead.

status.description: Where it is in its lifecycle.

oneOf.description: The cursor for the next page, if there is one.

limit.description: Lease at most this many messages, 1 to 100. Defaults to 1.

wait.description: If nothing is due, wait up to this long (at most 30s) for a message.

PushSettings.description: Where and how to push messages from a queue.

concurrency.description: How many requests to have in flight at once, per server.

secret.description: When set, each request is signed with HMAC-SHA256 using this secret.

timeout.description: How long to wait for the endpoint to respond.

url.description: The endpoint that receives each message as a POST request.

allOf.description: How messages in this queue are delivered.

Queue.description: A queue as stored, with its settings.

QueueName.description:
The name of a queue: 1 to 100 ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `_` or `.`.

The character set is deliberately small so names are safe in URLs, Redis
keys and metric labels without escaping.

QueueSettings.description:
The settings of a queue. Every field has a default, so a queue created
implicitly by scheduling a message works without configuration.

backoff.description: How long to wait before retrying a failed attempt.

max_attempts.description: How many times a message is attempted before it is marked dead.

paused.description: A paused queue accepts new messages but delivers none.

oneOf.description:
When set, the server delivers messages by POSTing them to this endpoint
instead of waiting for workers to poll.

retention.description:
How long finished messages are kept before they are deleted. This is
also how long idempotency keys are remembered.

visibility_timeout.description:
How long a lease lasts. A message that is not acked or nacked in this
time is handed to another worker.

QueueStats.description: How many messages a queue holds in each status.

scheduled.description: Waiting to run, now or later.

QueueSummary.description: A queue together with its message counts.

delay.description: Run after this delay. Cannot be combined with `run_at`.

run_at.description: Run at this time. With neither field, the message runs now.

ids.description: Only these messages. Without it, every dead message in the queue.

ScheduleBody.description: One message, or an array of up to 100.

ScheduleRequest.description: A request to schedule a message, as clients send it.

delay.description: Run after this delay. Cannot be combined with `run_at`.

idempotency_key.description:
Scheduling twice with the same key in the same queue creates only one
message.

max_attempts.description: Overrides the queue's `max_attempts` for this message.

priority.description: Higher priorities are delivered first. Defaults to 0.

run_at.description: Run at this time. Cannot be combined with `delay`.

visibility_timeout.description: Overrides the queue's `visibility_timeout` for this message.

ScheduleResponse.description: The message for a single schedule, or the results in order for a batch.

Scheduled.description: The result of scheduling one message.

created.description: False when a message with the same idempotency key already existed.

message.description:
The stored message: the new one, or the existing one with the same
idempotency key.

Status.description: Where a message is in its lifecycle. See `docs/design.md` for the diagram.
